title: Deploy or update PIM Manager (deploy everything)
purpose: Deploy or update the whole of PIM Manager in your own Azure subscription in one run: the hosting resources, the container image, the containers and their identities, the database schema, the mail sender, sign-in, the code, the nightly updater and the first administrators -- then verify it. Without -Apply it only prints the plan.
whenToRun: To install PIM Manager into a subscription from the downloaded package, or to bring an existing installation up to date with the same parameters. The guided install (Install-PimManager.ps1) runs it for you; run it directly when you deploy by hand or from your own pipeline. Run it with -WhatIf (or without -Apply) first.

runAs.name: Owner
runAs.why: It creates the resource group and every resource in it and assigns Azure roles to the identities it creates (Contributor + User Access Administrator is the equivalent).

runAs.name: User Access Administrator
runAs.scope: the target subscription (with Contributor, instead of Owner)
runAs.why: Azure role assignments for the managed identities (AcrPull, Reader, Contributor for the updater).

runAs.name: Owner or User Access Administrator at the tenant root management group
runAs.why: Only for the engine's Reader at the tenant root, so it can see every subscription. Without it the step warns and prints the command for the person who has it (Grant-PimEnginePermissions.ps1).

runAs.name: Privileged Role Administrator
runAs.why: Grants the Microsoft Graph application permissions to the engine and Manager identities and adds members to the role-assignable SQL admin group. Global Administrator also works.

runAs.name: Application Administrator
runAs.why: Creates the engine app registration and the Manager's sign-in app registration and consents the sign-in scopes. Cloud Application Administrator works for the registrations, not for the consent of Graph application permissions.

runAs.name: Groups Administrator
runAs.why: Creates the SQL admin group and the Manager's members-only sign-in group.

runAs.name: Exchange Administrator
runAs.why: Only for the mail sender step (shared mailbox + scoped send right). Without it the step is skipped with a warning and the command for the right person.

runAs.name: Azure CLI signed in (az login) as yourself, or a certificate deploy identity
runAs.why: Every call is pinned to -TenantId / -SubscriptionId; a signed-in run (-UseSignedInAccount) refuses a service principal, another tenant and another subscription.

changes.object: enrollment of this tenant (only with -EnrollmentKey)
changes.why: Links the installation to your Invardia account: Invardia creates the environment, signs the licence and issues an install key.
changes.undo: Ask Invardia support to remove the environment.

changes.object: deploy identity app registration with a certificate (only when no -AdminAppId and not -UseSignedInAccount; New-PimDeployIdentity.ps1)
changes.why: A one-shot deploy needs an identity that can create the hosting resources unattended.
changes.undo: Delete the app registration 'pim-deploy' and its certificate (Cert:\CurrentUser\My, subject CN=pim-deploy-<tenant>).

changes.object: deploy identity
changes.permission: Owner (Network Contributor on the hub virtual network when a hub is named)
changes.scope: the target subscription (the hub virtual network)
changes.why: It builds the resource group and assigns roles inside it; peering needs rights on the hub.
changes.undo: Remove the role assignments of the deploy identity.

changes.object: deploy identity (only with New-PimDeployIdentity -GrantGraph)
changes.why: Lets an unattended deploy identity create the sign-in app, converge the SQL admin group and consent the sign-in scopes.
changes.undo: Remove the app role assignments from the deploy identity's service principal (Enterprise applications > Permissions).

changes.object: engine app registration + service principal with a certificate credential (step appreg; not with -SkipAppReg)
changes.why: The identity the engine uses outside the containers (and the managing tenant cross-tenant).
changes.undo: Delete the app registration; remove the certificate CN=PIM4EntraPS-Engine from the machine store.

changes.object: engine app service principal (Install-PimEngineAppRegistration -IncludeExchange only; this deploy does NOT pass it)
changes.permission: Exchange.ManageAsApp (application) + Exchange Administrator activated time-bound through PIM
changes.why: Only for an engine that manages Exchange; documented because the installer the step runs can do it.
changes.undo: Remove the app role assignment; the PIM activation expires by itself.

changes.object: engine app service principal and the tick job's managed identity (the engine set)
changes.permission: Directory.Read.All, User.ReadWrite.All, Group.ReadWrite.All, RoleEligibilitySchedule.ReadWrite.Directory, RoleEligibilitySchedule.Remove.Directory, RoleAssignmentSchedule.ReadWrite.Directory, RoleAssignmentSchedule.Remove.Directory, RoleManagement.Read.All, RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory, RoleManagementPolicy.Read.Directory, RoleManagementPolicy.ReadWrite.Directory, RoleManagementPolicy.Read.AzureADGroup, RoleManagementPolicy.ReadWrite.AzureADGroup, PrivilegedAccess.ReadWrite.AzureADGroup, PrivilegedEligibilitySchedule.ReadWrite.AzureADGroup, PrivilegedEligibilitySchedule.Remove.AzureADGroup, PrivilegedAssignmentSchedule.ReadWrite.AzureADGroup, PrivilegedAssignmentSchedule.Remove.AzureADGroup, AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All, Application.Read.All, RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Defender, DeviceManagementRBAC.ReadWrite.All, AccessReview.Read.All, AccessReview.ReadWrite.All, AdministrativeUnit.ReadWrite.All, UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite.All, Domain.Read.All, Policy.Read.All (application permissions, admin consent)
changes.why: What the engine needs to apply the access you define: role and group assignments (eligible and active), role-assignable groups, administrative units, Temporary Access Passes, Defender and Intune roles, access reviews. Mail.Send is never granted tenant-wide.
changes.undo: Remove the app role assignments (Enterprise applications > the identity > Permissions), or delete the identity.

changes.object: the Manager's managed identity (the read-only set)
changes.permission: Directory.Read.All, Domain.Read.All, User.Read.All, Group.Read.All, AdministrativeUnit.Read.All, Application.Read.All, AccessReview.Read.All, RoleManagement.Read.All, RoleManagementPolicy.Read.Directory, RoleManagementPolicy.Read.AzureADGroup, RoleEligibilitySchedule.Read.Directory, RoleAssignmentSchedule.Read.Directory, PrivilegedAccess.Read.AzureADGroup, PrivilegedEligibilitySchedule.Read.AzureADGroup, PrivilegedAssignmentSchedule.Read.AzureADGroup (application)
changes.why: The Manager only reads; every change is queued and applied by the engine.
changes.undo: Remove the app role assignments of the Manager identity.

changes.object: resource group, virtual network + subnet (delegated to Container Apps), container registry, Log Analytics workspace, user-assigned pull identity, Azure SQL server + database (step prereq; New-PimHostingPrerequisites.ps1)
changes.why: Everything PIM Manager runs on, in your own subscription.
changes.undo: Delete the resource group (this deletes the database: export it first).

changes.object: the pull identity, the containers and the jobs
changes.why: The containers pull their image without registry passwords.
changes.undo: Remove the AcrPull role assignments on the registry.

changes.object: group grp-pim-sql-admins (role-assignable) as the SQL server's Entra admin, with the environment identities and the Invardia Support app (when named) as members
changes.why: One admin group for the store; role-assignable so a Groups Administrator or User Administrator cannot add themselves to it.
changes.undo: Set another Entra admin on the SQL server, then delete the group.

changes.object: the person running a signed-in deploy
changes.why: The store steps connect to SQL as that person; Azure SQL is Entra-only.
changes.undo: Remove the person from the group.

changes.object: firewall rule AllowSetupHost for this machine's public IP (read from api.ipify.org unless -SetupHostIp)
changes.why: The schema, settings and access steps connect from this machine.
changes.undo: Removed by the run at its end; otherwise: az sql server firewall-rule delete -n AllowSetupHost.

changes.object: container image pim-manager:<version> built in your registry (step image; az acr build from the package's source)
changes.why: The image is built from the code you downloaded, in your own registry.
changes.undo: Delete the repository in the registry.

changes.object: Container Apps environment, the Manager app ca-pim-manager, the tick job ca-pim-tick, the bootstrap job ca-pim-dbinit, their system / user-assigned managed identities (step infra; Setup-PimContainers.ps1)
changes.why: The runtime: the Manager (GUI) and the engine, on a schedule.
changes.undo: Delete the apps, the jobs and the environment (or the resource group).

changes.object: the tick job's managed identity (the Manager gets Reader only)
changes.why: So the engine can see the Azure resources whose roles you manage.
changes.undo: Remove the role assignment.

changes.object: the tick job's managed identity
changes.permission: Reader (+ User Access Administrator only with -EngineAzureRootUserAccessAdmin)
changes.why: Discovery across every subscription; User Access Administrator only when the engine must assign the Azure roles you delegate.
changes.undo: Remove the role assignment at the tenant root management group.

changes.object: database users (CREATE USER from each identity's application id) for ca-pim-manager, ca-pim-tick, the updater and the support user
changes.permission: db_datareader, db_datawriter, db_ddladmin (ALTER ROLE ... ADD MEMBER)
changes.why: The containers read and write the store and apply the schema.
changes.undo: DROP USER [<name>] in the database.

changes.object: subnet service endpoint Microsoft.Sql + a virtual network rule on the SQL server (step sqlaccess; Set-PimSqlNetworkAccess.ps1)
changes.why: The containers reach SQL from their own subnet.
changes.undo: Remove the virtual network rule and the service endpoint.

changes.object: the PIM schema (step schema; idempotent, never destructive)
changes.why: Tables and columns the version needs.
changes.undo: Restore the database from its point-in-time backup.

changes.object: shared sender mailbox, an Exchange service principal per sending identity (New-ServicePrincipal), a management scope for that one mailbox (New-ManagementScope), the scoped role assignment 'Application Mail.Send' (New-ManagementRoleAssignment), a shared mailbox (New-Mailbox) when absent (step mailsender; Initialize-PimMailSender.ps1)
changes.why: Notification mail is sent by the solution's own identities, from one mailbox only.
changes.undo: Remove-ManagementRoleAssignment, Remove-ManagementScope, then remove the mailbox.

changes.object: the Manager and tick identities
changes.why: They can send only as that mailbox; a tenant-wide Mail.Send found on them is revoked.
changes.undo: Remove-ManagementRoleAssignment for the identity.

changes.object: a tenant-wide Mail.Send application permission on the sending identities, if one exists
changes.why: A tenant-wide Mail.Send would bypass the mailbox scope.
changes.undo: Grant it again (not recommended).

changes.object: pim.Settings feature gates scheduler.jobs, alerting.email, msp.downlink ON (step features)
changes.why: A deployed engine with its gates off does nothing.
changes.undo: Turn the gates off in Settings or with Set-PimFeatureBaseline.ps1.

changes.object: the Manager's sign-in app registration ('PIM4EntraPS Manager'), its client secret (stored only as a secret of the container app), and a members-only dynamic group when every member account may sign in (step easyauth; Set-PimManagerEasyAuth.ps1)
changes.why: Sign-in in front of the Manager; nobody reaches it without an Entra sign-in.
changes.undo: Remove Easy Auth from the container app and delete the app registration and the group.

changes.object: the Manager's sign-in app
changes.permission: openid, profile, email, User.Read (delegated, admin consent via oauth2PermissionGrants)
changes.why: So people can sign in without a consent prompt.
changes.undo: Remove the consent (Enterprise applications > the app > Permissions).

changes.object: the people / groups in -EasyAuthAllowedPrincipals (or the members-only group)
changes.permission: app role assignment on the sign-in app (appRoleAssignedTo), assignment required
changes.why: Only the named people may sign in.
changes.undo: Remove the assignments, or set assignment required off.

changes.object: the Manager app and the jobs rolled to the new image (step code)
changes.why: The new version runs.
changes.undo: Roll back to the previous revision (the deploy does this itself when verify fails).

changes.object: nightly updater job ca-pim-update with its managed identity (step updater; Deploy-PimUpdateJob.ps1)
changes.why: The installation keeps itself up to date on its ring.
changes.undo: Delete the job (Enable-PimSelfUpdate / -SkipUpdater on a re-run).

changes.object: the updater job's managed identity
changes.permission: Contributor (+ AcrPull on the registry, Contributor on the registry when it lives in another resource group)
changes.scope: the PIM resource group (and the registry)
changes.why: It rolls the container apps and builds the image of an approved version.
changes.undo: Remove the role assignments; delete the job.

changes.object: the updater job's managed identity
changes.why: It applies the schema of the version it rolls to.
changes.undo: Remove it from the group.

changes.object: pim.Settings ManagerAccess: the -ManagerSuperAdmins as SuperAdmin (step access; Set-PimManagerAccess.ps1)
changes.why: A new environment needs someone who can administer it.
changes.undo: Change the access in Settings > Access.

changes.object: pim.Settings Alerting recipients when empty (step alerting; Set-PimAlertRecipients.ps1)
changes.why: Someone receives the alerts from day one.
changes.undo: Edit them in Settings.

changes.object: pim.Settings License + InvardiaInstallKey (step licence, only with an enrollment; Set-PimLicense.ps1)
changes.why: Registers the licence the enrollment returned.
changes.undo: Remove the licence in Settings > Licence.

changes.object: the deploy profile (parameters of a successful -Apply, never a secret) for Update-PimCommunity.ps1, in your profile folder
changes.why: So a later update can re-run exactly this deploy.
changes.undo: Delete the profile file printed at the end.

readsOnly: Plan-only facts: the app registration, resource group, registry, pull identity and its AcrPull, SQL server and its Entra admin, Container Apps environment, apps, jobs, their Graph app role assignments (application permission reads), Azure role assignments, peering state, image tags.

The signed-in account (az account show) and its token, checked for tenant and user-ness; directory role checks name Global Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator, Application Administrator, Cloud Application Administrator, Groups Administrator, User Administrator, Exchange Administrator only to report what is missing.
The deployed database columns (schema drift detect) and the running image's content hash.
Database role memberships it checks against (db_owner, db_securityadmin, db_accessadmin, db_backupoperator, db_denydatareader, db_denydatawriter are never granted by the deploy).
Exchange (read): Get-Mailbox, Get-ManagementScope, Get-ManagementRoleAssignment, Get-ServicePrincipal; Organization.Read.All for the mail check.
SQL GRANT SELECT / GRANT INSERT, UPDATE on single tables for special-purpose users (the publish and support readers) are only made by the managing-tenant build steps, not by this deploy.
network: outlook.office365.com (Exchange Online admin API, mail sender step)
invardia.com (only with -EnrollmentKey or a tracked install)

the Azure CLI extension index (azcliextensionsync.blob.core.windows.net): az installs its 'containerapp' extension once when it is missing (extension.use_dynamic_install, set by the prerequisite / container / image steps) -- az's own download, checked against the index's sha256
the update source URL (-UpdateSourceUrlTemplate), fetched by the updater job in Azure -- not by this script
whatIf: Prints the ordered plan (every step: run, current, not applicable) and, under it, each change a step marked to run would make (object, permission, scope) -- for example '[infra] Microsoft Graph application permissions -> ca-pim-tick identity (the engine set) @ tenant'. Plan-only reads only; -WhatIf wins over -Apply: no Invardia claim, no deploy identity, no firewall window, no step runs.
undo: Delete the resource group (export the database first), the Entra objects it created (engine app registration, the Manager's sign-in app, grp-pim-sql-admins, the members group), the role assignments at the tenant root management group, and the Exchange management role assignment, scope and mailbox. See each change's undo.
